title: Stieger et al. 2021 — Continuous sensorimotor rhythm based brain computer interface learning in a large population
description: A large longitudinal EEG dataset of sensorimotor rhythm (SMR) based brain-computer interface (BCI) learning. It contains over 600 hours of recordings from 62 healthy adults across up to 11 online training sessions. Participants performed continuous cursor control in three tasks (LR, UD, 2D) using four motor-imagery classes (left hand, right hand, both hands, rest). The data support the design, evaluation and improvement of BCI algorithms.
methods_description: Participants completed 7-11 online BCI training sessions of 450 trials each, spanning three tasks (LR, UD, 2D) in 6 runs. EEG was recorded with 62 channels using Neuroscan SynAmps RT amplifiers at 1000 Hz. Online control used Laplacian spatial filtering around C3/C4 and an autoregressive spectral estimate (order 16). The control signal was alpha power (12 Hz ± 1.5 Hz): horizontal cursor motion was driven by lateralized alpha power (C4-C3) and vertical motion by total alpha power (C4+C3). Control signals were normalized to zero mean and unit variance, and the cursor position was updated every 40 ms.
